title: Yogurt and raspberry swirl
summary: Plain whole-milk yogurt with mashed raspberries: a two-minute way to introduce dairy, no added sugar needed.
texture: Smooth, with the raspberries mashed and pressed through a sieve so there are no seeds or lumps for first tastes.
steps: Mash the raspberries with a fork, then press them through a fine sieve to remove the seeds.
Swirl the raspberry puree through the yogurt.
Offer on a spoon. Serve cold or at room temperature.
choking: Mash the raspberries fully. Sieving out the seeds keeps the texture smooth for new eaters.

allergens.name: Milk
allergens.note: Yogurt is a great first dairy food: cow's milk products like yogurt and cheese can be introduced before 12 months, even though cow's milk as a drink waits until 12 months.

storage: Best mixed fresh. Plain yogurt keeps in the fridge until its use-by date once opened, usually about a week.
tips: Choose plain, unsweetened, whole-milk yogurt. Flavored and 'kids' yogurts often have a lot of added sugar.
Swap raspberries for mashed ripe banana, peach or mango.
